COUNTY OF CHESTER. WEIGHTS AND MEASURES ACTS. 1878 AND 1889. APPOINTMENT OF INSPECTORS OF WEIGHTS ANT,' MEASURES, .•••••••• rrtlE Weights and Measure* Committee of tha JL Cheshire County Council are desirous of appointing One Chief Inapector and Three Bub-Inspectors, and are prepared to receive applications by persons seeking the appointment. The persons appointed must be prepared subsequent to their appointment and within two months thereof to pass the first Examination held by the Board of Trade qualifying them to perform such duties, and they will also be required to act as Inspectors under the Food and Drugs Act and per- form such other duties as the County Council may from time to time delegate to them. The salary of the Chief Inspector .will be £250 per annum, and the salary of each of the three Sub-Inspoctors will be £175 per annum payable quarterly, such salaries to com- mence on their respectively passing the Board of Trade Examination, and to include all expenses other than the actual cost of travelling in the performance of their duties, the hire of rooms for verification. Ac., and the conveyance of Local Standards and any assistance which in the opinion of the Committee is necessary in connection. with such con- veyance. They will be required to devote the whole of tiler time to the service of the County, and to reside in such parts of the County as the Committee may decide. They will hold office subject to three calendar months notice on either side, and which may be given at any time of the year, and they will not be entitled to any superannuation allowance or compensation, whether authorized by Act of Parliament or otherwise, on their services being dispensed with. They will be required to enter into recognizances and give such other security as the Committee may decide for the due and faithful performance of their duties. Applications in applicant's hanctwriting stating age (which is not to exceed 40 years). qualifications, &c., together with three recent testimonials are to be sent to the Clerk of the County Council, Chefter, so that the same may be received by him on or before the 17th day of May is tent. Plans M the Districts can be inspected at the Clerk's Office. Canvassing, whether personally or by letter, is prohibited. Dated this 6th day of May, 1890 REGINALD POTTS, Clerk of the County Council.

Total WARRINGTON v. WIGAN. The inauguration of the cricket season in Warrington district took place on Saturday, when the Warrington and Wigan teams met on the Arpley ground. Owing to the counter atti action of the football match, the atten- dance was not so large as usual,. only about 200 persons witnessing the game. The Wamngtonians opened to the deliveries of Macattlq and Rennick, Messrs. S. M. and S. J. Crosfield being the batsmen. So capital was the de- fence that, despite several changes in the bowling, the total reached 60 ere the home captain was disposed of. Lawton came next, but a smart catch by Hunter caused his dismissal. Smith, on coming in, treated the specta- tors to some fine hitting. A few strokes sufficed for his running up 27, and then he failed to stop a straight ball delivered by Macauley. "J. J." was dismissed in a similar manner to the home captain, a capital catch by Rennick causing his retirement to the pavilion. Arm- strong and Wagstaffe gave little trouble, but Podmore, who is an established favourite with the home suppor- ters, caused a surprise by putting 32 together, though he gave several distinct chances. Voisey contributed /1 runs, but none of the ether players rendered much assis- tance, the final score being 158. Wigan opened their in- nings with Rennick and Wall to the deliveries of Adams and Smith, and in an hour and a quarter the whole set were dismisSed for a score of 87, leaving Warrington vic- torious by a majority of 71 runs. Captain Adams' figures read remarkably well, as in 19 overs he took six wickets for 39 runs. The fielding all round was good. WARRINOTSN I WIGAN. I SOUTH-WEST LANCASHIRE JUVENILE TEMPLA.B S. The quarterly session of the South-west Lanca- shire District Juvenile Council was held in the Co-operative Hall, Earlestown, on Saturday after- noon. There was a large attendance of representa- tives from all parts of the district, and Bro. Arthur Nswell,'D.S.J.T., of Liverpool, presided. He was supported by the district officers. In his report the teferred to the work of the order and stated that there had been an increase in the membership during the quarter. In closing the report Bro. Nowell intimated that owing to continued ill-health he was com- pelled to resign the post of D.S.J.T.—The report was acceptecl,as IRS also that of the District Treasurer, which showed the finances to be in satisfactory condition, In the course of the buainem which folloWed a vote of con- dolence and sympathy with 81ster Pickersgs t!- 011 tbe death of her husband, Bro. J. Pickersgill, D.E.S., was unanimously passed. A resolution protesting against compensation to publicans was adopted, and the resigna- tion of Bro. Newell was accepted with an expression of regret. In regard to the next quarterly meeting it was decided to communicate with the West Cheshire District Council with the view of arranging for a joint meeting at Egremont, Sea,combe, or New Brighton. The session terminated with a vote of thanks to the members of the Earlestown Lodge for their Occellent arrangements.—A public tea meeting followed, and about 80 sat down to tea. 'At the subsequent proceedings, Bro. A. Newell (Liverpool), presided. The hall was well filled. The Rev. J. Bennett Anderson, of Liverpool, gave an interesting address, and during the evening, a pro- gramme of songs, recitations, &c., was rendered by the following members of the Pride of Earlestown Juvenile Templar Brothers :—A. Warburton, W. Marshall, and E. Jones ; Sister T. Marshall,. Miss Sutherland (Hindley), and Mr. Sutherland.
